The test image shows tomato leaves with a pale, silvery-white powdery coating across the leaf surface. Leaves look bleached/silvery-green with a dusty white appearance on the upper surface. No distinct spots with defined margins. This strongly suggests Powdery Mildew.

Now viewing one reference image for confirmation:

The reference Powdery Mildew image shows discrete white powdery patches on green leaves (early stage). The test image appears to show more advanced/widespread silvery-white coating across the entire leaf surface, which is consistent with advanced Powdery Mildew where white fungal growth covers most of the leaf area, causing the bleached/silvery appearance. No other disease class fits the uniform whitish dusty coating observed.
